A = θ r^{2}.title: Area of a circular sector
A = θ r^{2}.about: A sector of radius r that spans ±θ either side of its symmetry axis (total angle 2θ) has area θr^{2}. Multiply by the areal density to get the mass that goes into the inertia formulas.
assumptions: θ is the half-angle, in radians; the full opening is 2θ
θ = π gives the whole disk, πr^{2}; θ = π/2 gives the half disk

example.problem: A 60° pie slice (half-angle θ = 30° = π/6) is cut from a disk of radius 0.3 m. Find its area.

y_{cm} = 2r sin(θ)/(3θ).title: Mass centre of a circular sector
y_{cm} = 2r sin(θ)/(3θ).about: The mass centre of a uniform sector lies on its symmetry axis, a distance 2r sin(θ)/(3θ) from the apex (the circle's centre). You need it to move inertia from the apex to the mass centre.
assumptions: θ is the half-angle in radians
Uniform density (for a plate or shell: uniform mass per area)
As θ → 0 it tends to 2r/3, the centroid of a thin triangle
vars: distance from the apex to the mass centre, along the symmetry axis
related: thin arc of the same angle

example.problem: Where is the mass centre of a 60° pie slice (θ = π/6) of radius 0.3 m?

I_{xx} = (1/4) m r^{2} [1 + sin(2θ)/(2θ).title: Sector: moment of inertia across its symmetry axis
I_{xx} = (1/4) m r^{2} [1 + sin(2θ)/(2θ).about: The moment of inertia of a uniform sector about the x axis through its mass centre, perpendicular to the symmetry axis y and in the plane. The last term is the parallel-axis correction from the apex to the mass centre.
assumptions: θ is the half-angle in radians
Axes pass through the mass centre B_{cm}, as drawn; for a parallel axis at distance d add m d^{2}
Thin flat plate: thickness ignored
About the apex instead, drop the last term: (1/4) m r^{2} [1 + sin(2θ)/(2θ)]
vars: moment of inertia about x through B_{cm}

example.problem: A 2 kg quarter-disk plate (θ = π/4) has radius 0.3 m. Find I_{xx} about its mass centre.

I_{yy} = (1/4) m r^{2} [1 − sin(2θ)/(2θ).title: Sector: moment of inertia about its symmetry axis
I_{yy} = (1/4) m r^{2} [1 − sin(2θ)/(2θ).about: The moment of inertia of a uniform sector about its symmetry axis y. That axis runs through the apex and the mass centre alike, so no parallel-axis term appears.
assumptions: θ is the half-angle in radians
Thin flat plate
θ = π gives the full disk, (1/4) m r^{2}
vars: moment of inertia about the symmetry axis
related: across the symmetry axis, at B_{cm}

example.problem: A 2 kg quarter-disk plate (θ = π/4) has radius 0.3 m. Find I_{yy} about its symmetry axis.

A = (1/2) π r^{2}.title: Area of a half disk
A = (1/2) π r^{2}.about: A semicircular plate (half disk) of radius r has half the area of the full disk. It is the sector with half-angle θ = π/2.
assumptions: Flat, thin plate
Mass m = ρ_{A} A for areal density ρ_{A}
related: mass centre from the flat edge

example.problem: Find the area of a half disk of radius 0.25 m.

y_{cm} = 4r/(3π).title: Mass centre of a half disk
y_{cm} = 4r/(3π).about: The mass centre of a uniform half disk lies on its symmetry axis at 4r/(3π) ≈ 0.424 r from the flat edge (the centre of the full circle).
assumptions: Uniform density (for a plate or shell: uniform mass per area)
Measured from the straight edge, along the symmetry axis
vars: distance from the flat edge to the mass centre
related: general sector; θ = π/2 gives this

example.problem: How far from its flat edge is the mass centre of a half disk of radius 0.25 m?

I_{xx} = (1/4) m r^{2} (1 − 64/(9π^{2})).title: Half disk: inertia about the axis parallel to the flat edge
I_{xx} = (1/4) m r^{2} (1 − 64/(9π^{2})).about: The moment of inertia of a uniform half disk about the x axis through its mass centre, parallel to the flat edge. It is (1/4) m r^{2} about the edge, less m y_{cm}^{2} to move to the mass centre.
assumptions: Axes pass through the mass centre B_{cm}, as drawn; for a parallel axis at distance d add m d^{2}
Thin plate
About the flat edge itself: (1/4) m r^{2}
vars: moment of inertia about x through B_{cm}
related: parallel-axis theorem: shift to an axis a distance d away

example.problem: A 3 kg half-disk plate has radius 0.25 m. Find I_{xx} about its mass centre.

I_{yy} = (1/4) m r^{2}.title: Half disk: inertia about its symmetry axis
I_{yy} = (1/4) m r^{2}.about: The moment of inertia of a uniform half disk about its symmetry axis y, which is perpendicular to the flat edge. It is the same (1/4) m r^{2} as a full disk, since each half contributes equally.
assumptions: Thin plate
The y axis passes through the mass centre and the edge's midpoint alike
vars: moment of inertia about the symmetry axis
related: parallel to the edge, at B_{cm}

example.problem: A 3 kg half-disk plate has radius 0.25 m. Find I_{yy}.

I_{zz} = (1/2) m r^{2} (1 − 32/(9π^{2})).title: Half disk: inertia normal to the plate
I_{zz} = (1/2) m r^{2} (1 − 32/(9π^{2})).about: The moment of inertia of a uniform half disk about the z axis through its mass centre, normal to the plate. It equals I_{xx} + I_{yy}.
assumptions: Axes pass through the mass centre B_{cm}, as drawn; for a parallel axis at distance d add m d^{2}
Thin plate
About the centre of the flat edge: (1/2) m r^{2}
vars: moment of inertia normal to the plate through B_{cm}
related: perpendicular-axis theorem for a flat body in the xy plane
mass centre from the flat edge
parallel-axis theorem: shift to an axis a distance d away

example.problem: A 3 kg half-disk plate has radius 0.25 m. Find I_{zz} about its mass centre.

A = π r^{2}.title: Area of a disk
A = π r^{2}.about: The area of a circular disk of radius r. For a thin plate, mass = areal density × A.
assumptions: Flat, thin plate of uniform thickness

example.problem: A steel disk 1.5 mm thick (ρ = 7850 kg/m^{3}) has radius 0.15 m. Find its area and mass.

I_{xx} = I_{yy} = (1/4) m r^{2}.title: Thin disk: inertia about a diameter
I_{xx} = I_{yy} = (1/4) m r^{2}.about: A thin uniform disk has moment of inertia (1/4) m r^{2} about any diameter. It is half the polar value by the perpendicular-axis theorem and symmetry.
assumptions: Thin: for a disk of thickness h use the cylinder, (1/12) m (3r^{2} + h^{2})
Axes through the centre, in the plane of the disk
vars: moment of inertia about a diameter
related: perpendicular-axis theorem for a flat body in the xy plane

example.problem: A 4 kg thin disk of radius 0.15 m wobbles about a diameter. Find I_{xx}.

I_{zz} = (1/2) m r^{2}.title: Disk or solid cylinder: inertia about its axis
I_{zz} = (1/2) m r^{2}.about: A uniform disk or solid cylinder has moment of inertia (1/2) m r^{2} about its central axis, whatever its length. It is the inertia of a flywheel, pulley or wheel spinning on its axle.
assumptions: Uniform density; a rim-heavy wheel is nearer m r^{2}
About the axis of symmetry through the centre
vars: moment of inertia about the axle

example.problem: A 4 kg disk of radius 0.15 m spins at 300 rpm. Find I_{zz} and its kinetic energy.

x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2}.title: Edge of a disk
x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2}.about: A point Q = x b̂_{x} + y b̂_{y} lies on the rim of the disk when its coordinates satisfy x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2}. Points inside have x^{2} + y^{2} < r^{2}.
assumptions: x, y measured from the disk's centre on body axes b̂_{x}, b̂_{y} in the plane of the disk
vars: coordinates of Q from the centre
related: x = r cos(φ), y = r sin(φ)
the rim in terms of the angle φ

example.problem: A rim point of a disk of radius 0.2 m has x = 0.12 m. Find y.

A = π a b.title: Area of an ellipse
A = π a b.about: A flat ellipse with semi-axes a (along x) and b (along y) has area πab. With a = b = r it is the disk, πr^{2}.
assumptions: a and b are semi-axes (half the full widths)

example.problem: An elliptical plate is 0.6 m by 0.4 m overall. Find its area.

I_{xx} = (1/4) m b^{2}.title: Elliptical plate: inertia about the x axis
I_{xx} = (1/4) m b^{2}.about: A thin uniform elliptical plate has moment of inertia (1/4) m b^{2} about its x axis (the a axis). Only the spread in y, set by b, counts.
assumptions: Thin plate; axes through the centre
x lies along semi-axis a, y along b

example.problem: A 1.5 kg elliptical plate has a = 0.3 m and b = 0.2 m. Find I_{xx}.

I_{yy} = (1/4) m a^{2}.title: Elliptical plate: inertia about the y axis
I_{yy} = (1/4) m a^{2}.about: A thin uniform elliptical plate has moment of inertia (1/4) m a^{2} about its y axis (the b axis). Only the spread in x, set by a, counts.
assumptions: Thin plate; axes through the centre
x lies along semi-axis a, y along b

example.problem: A 1.5 kg elliptical plate has a = 0.3 m and b = 0.2 m. Find I_{yy} and I_{zz}.

A = a b.title: Area of a rectangular plate
A = a b.about: A rectangle of width a (along x) and height b (along y) has area ab.
assumptions: a and b are full side lengths

example.problem: A 3 mm aluminium sheet (ρ = 2700 kg/m^{3}) is 0.4 m by 0.3 m. Find its area and mass.

I_{xx} = (1/12) m b^{2}.title: Rectangular plate: inertia about the x axis
I_{xx} = (1/12) m b^{2}.about: A thin uniform rectangular plate has moment of inertia (1/12) m b^{2} about the x axis through its centre, where b is the side across that axis. It is the slender-rod result, since the width a along the axis does not matter.
assumptions: Thin plate; axes through the mass centre, parallel to the sides
About an edge instead: (1/3) m b^{2}
vars: side along y (across the x axis)

example.problem: A 2 kg plate is 0.4 m along x and 0.3 m along y. Find I_{xx}.

I_{yy} = (1/12) m a^{2}.title: Rectangular plate: inertia about the y axis
I_{yy} = (1/12) m a^{2}.about: A thin uniform rectangular plate has moment of inertia (1/12) m a^{2} about the y axis through its centre, where a is the side across that axis.
assumptions: Thin plate; axes through the mass centre, parallel to the sides
A door hinged along its edge: (1/3) m a^{2}
vars: side along x (across the y axis)
related: parallel-axis theorem: shift to an axis a distance d away

example.problem: A 2 kg plate is 0.4 m along x and 0.3 m along y. Find I_{yy}, and I_{zz}.

V = π r^{2} h.title: Volume of a solid cylinder
V = π r^{2} h.about: A solid circular cylinder of radius r and length h has volume πr^{2}h. Multiply by density for its mass.
assumptions: Right circular cylinder, flat ends

example.problem: A steel bar (ρ = 7850 kg/m^{3}) is 0.4 m long and 0.1 m in diameter. Find its volume and mass.

I_{xx} = I_{yy} = (1/12) m (3r^{2} + h^{.title: Solid cylinder: inertia about a transverse axis
I_{xx} = I_{yy} = (1/12) m (3r^{2} + h^{.about: A uniform solid cylinder has moment of inertia (1/12) m (3r^{2} + h^{2}) about any axis through its mass centre perpendicular to its length. It spans from the thin disk (h → 0) to the slender rod (r → 0).
assumptions: Axes through the mass centre, perpendicular to the cylinder's axis z
About an end face's diameter add m (h/2)^{2}
vars: moment of inertia about a transverse axis through B_{cm}
related: parallel-axis theorem: shift to an axis a distance d away

example.problem: A 5 kg solid cylinder has radius 0.05 m and length 0.4 m. Find I_{xx} about its mass centre.

V = π (r_{o}^{2} − r_{i}^{2}) h.title: Volume of a thick-walled tube
V = π (r_{o}^{2} − r_{i}^{2}) h.about: A tube of outer radius r_{o}, inner radius r_{i} and length h has the volume of the outer cylinder minus the hole.
assumptions: Concentric circular bore, flat ends

example.problem: A tube is 0.3 m long with r_{o} = 60 mm and r_{i} = 40 mm. Find the volume of material.

I_{xx} = I_{yy} = (1/12) m [3(r_{o}^{2}.title: Thick tube: inertia about a transverse axis
I_{xx} = I_{yy} = (1/12) m [3(r_{o}^{2}.about: A uniform thick-walled tube has moment of inertia (1/12) m [3(r_{o}^{2} + r_{i}^{2}) + h^{2}] about a transverse axis through its mass centre. r_{i} = 0 gives the solid cylinder.
assumptions: Axes through the mass centre, perpendicular to the tube's axis z
m is the mass of the material present (the hole removed)
vars: moment of inertia about a transverse axis through B_{cm}

example.problem: A 3 kg tube is 0.3 m long with r_{o} = 0.06 m and r_{i} = 0.04 m. Find I_{xx} about its mass centre.

I_{zz} = (1/2) m (r_{o}^{2} + r_{i}^{2}).title: Thick tube: inertia about its axis
I_{zz} = (1/2) m (r_{o}^{2} + r_{i}^{2}).about: A uniform thick-walled tube, ring or hub has moment of inertia (1/2) m (r_{o}^{2} + r_{i}^{2}) about its axis. Note the plus sign: m already accounts for the hole.
assumptions: m is the mass of the material present
r_{i} = 0 gives (1/2) m r^{2}; r_{i} → r_{o} gives the thin tube m r^{2}
vars: moment of inertia about the axis

example.problem: A 3 kg steel ring has r_{o} = 0.06 m and r_{i} = 0.04 m. Find its inertia about its axis.

A = 2π r h.title: Area of a thin-walled tube
A = 2π r h.about: The lateral (side) surface of a cylinder of radius r and length h has area 2πrh. For a thin-walled tube, mass = areal density × A.
assumptions: Side wall only; end caps not included (add 2πr^{2} for both)
Wall thickness t ≪ r; then V ≈ 2πrht

example.problem: A sheet-metal duct has radius 0.1 m and length 0.5 m. Find its wall area.

I_{xx} = I_{yy} = (1/12) m (6r^{2} + h^{.title: Thin-walled tube: inertia about a transverse axis
I_{xx} = I_{yy} = (1/12) m (6r^{2} + h^{.about: A thin-walled open tube has moment of inertia (1/12) m (6r^{2} + h^{2}) about a transverse axis through its mass centre. The 6r^{2} (vs 3r^{2} for a solid cylinder) reflects all the mass sitting at radius r.
assumptions: Wall thickness ≪ r; no end caps
Axes through the mass centre, perpendicular to the axis z
vars: moment of inertia about a transverse axis through B_{cm}
related: parallel-axis theorem: shift to an axis a distance d away

example.problem: A 2 kg thin-walled tube has radius 0.1 m and length 0.5 m. Find I_{xx} about its mass centre.

V = (1/3) π r^{2} h.title: Volume of a solid cone
V = (1/3) π r^{2} h.about: A solid right-circular cone of base radius r and height h has a third of the volume of the cylinder that encloses it.
assumptions: Right circular cone (apex over the base centre)

example.problem: Find the volume of a cone 0.3 m tall with a base radius of 0.1 m.

y_{cm} = h/4.title: Mass centre of a solid cone
y_{cm} = h/4.about: The mass centre of a uniform solid cone is on its axis, a quarter of the height above the base (three quarters down from the apex). Most of the volume is near the base.
assumptions: Uniform density (for a plate or shell: uniform mass per area)
Measured from the base along the axis y
vars: height of the mass centre above the base

example.problem: Where is the mass centre of a solid cone 0.3 m tall?

I_{xx} = I_{zz} = (3/80) m (4r^{2} + h^{.title: Solid cone: inertia about a transverse axis
I_{xx} = I_{zz} = (3/80) m (4r^{2} + h^{.about: A uniform solid cone has moment of inertia (3/80) m (4r^{2} + h^{2}) about any axis through its mass centre perpendicular to its axis y.
assumptions: Axes pass through the mass centre B_{cm}, as drawn; for a parallel axis at distance d add m d^{2} (the mass centre is h/4 above the base)
About the apex: (3/20) m (r^{2} + 4h^{2}); about a base diameter: (1/20) m (3r^{2} + 2h^{2})
vars: moment of inertia about a transverse axis through B_{cm}
related: parallel-axis theorem: shift to an axis a distance d away

example.problem: A 2 kg solid cone has base radius 0.1 m and height 0.3 m. Find I_{xx} about its mass centre.

I_{yy} = (3/10) m r^{2}.title: Solid cone: inertia about its axis
I_{yy} = (3/10) m r^{2}.about: A uniform solid cone has moment of inertia (3/10) m r^{2} about its axis of symmetry, less than a cylinder's (1/2) m r^{2} because the mass tapers toward the axis.
assumptions: Uniform density; any height
y is the cone's axis, through apex and base centre
vars: moment of inertia about the cone's axis

example.problem: A 2 kg solid cone with base radius 0.1 m spins on its axis like a top. Find I_{yy}.

A = π r √(r^{2} + h^{2}).title: Lateral area of a cone
A = π r √(r^{2} + h^{2}).about: The slanted surface of a cone of base radius r and height h has area π r s, where s = √(r^{2} + h^{2}) is the slant length. It is the area of a thin conical shell (a funnel or lampshade) with no base.
assumptions: Side surface only; add πr^{2} for a closed base
Thin wall: mass = areal density × A

example.problem: A sheet-metal hopper is a cone with base radius 0.3 m and height 0.4 m. Find its wall area.

y_{cm} = h/3.title: Mass centre of a thin-walled cone
y_{cm} = h/3.about: The mass centre of a uniform conical shell (no base) is on its axis, a third of the height above the base. It sits higher than the solid cone's h/4 because the shell has no mass filling the base.
assumptions: Uniform thin wall, no base
The same h/3 holds for the area centroid of a triangle
vars: height of the mass centre above the base

example.problem: Where is the mass centre of a lampshade cone 0.4 m tall?

I_{xx} = I_{zz} = m (r^{2}/4 + h^{2}/18).title: Thin-walled cone: inertia about a transverse axis
I_{xx} = I_{zz} = m (r^{2}/4 + h^{2}/18).about: A uniform conical shell without a base has moment of inertia m (r^{2}/4 + h^{2}/18) about an axis through its mass centre perpendicular to its axis.
assumptions: Axes pass through the mass centre B_{cm}, as drawn; for a parallel axis at distance d add m d^{2} (h/3 above the base)
Thin wall, no base
vars: moment of inertia about a transverse axis through B_{cm}
related: parallel-axis theorem: shift to an axis a distance d away

example.problem: A 1.2 kg conical shell has base radius 0.3 m and height 0.4 m. Find I_{xx} about its mass centre.

V = (1/2) π r^{2} a.title: Volume of a solid paraboloid
V = (1/2) π r^{2} a.about: A solid paraboloid of revolution with flat-face radius r and length a has half the volume of the cylinder that encloses it.
assumptions: Surface is a parabola revolved about the x axis; the flat face is at Bₒ, the vertex a away
vars: length from the flat face to the vertex
related: mass centre from the flat face
cone of the same size, for comparison

example.problem: A paraboloidal nose piece has r = 0.1 m and a = 0.2 m. Find its volume.

x_{cm} = a/3.title: Mass centre of a solid paraboloid
x_{cm} = a/3.about: The mass centre of a uniform solid paraboloid lies on its axis, a third of its length from the flat face Bₒ (two thirds from the vertex).
assumptions: Uniform density (for a plate or shell: uniform mass per area)
Measured along x from the flat face Bₒ
vars: distance from the flat face to the mass centre
length from flat face to vertex

example.problem: Where is the mass centre of a solid paraboloid 0.2 m long?
steps: x_{cm} = 0.2 m/3 = 0.0667 m from the flat face

I_{xx} = (1/3) m r^{2}.title: Solid paraboloid: inertia about its axis
I_{xx} = (1/3) m r^{2}.about: A uniform solid paraboloid has moment of inertia (1/3) m r^{2} about its axis of symmetry x. That axis runs through both Bₒ and the mass centre, so the value is the same at either.
assumptions: Uniform density
r is the radius of the flat face
vars: moment of inertia about the axis

example.problem: A 3 kg solid paraboloid has a flat-face radius of 0.1 m. Find I_{xx}.

I_{yy} = I_{zz} = (1/18) m (a^{2} + 3r^{.title: Solid paraboloid: transverse inertia at the mass centre
I_{yy} = I_{zz} = (1/18) m (a^{2} + 3r^{.about: A uniform solid paraboloid has moment of inertia (1/18) m (a^{2} + 3r^{2}) about any axis through its mass centre perpendicular to its axis x.
assumptions: Axes through the mass centre, a/3 from the flat face
About Bₒ instead add m (a/3)^{2}, giving (1/6) m (a^{2} + r^{2})
vars: moment of inertia about a transverse axis through B_{cm}
related: parallel-axis theorem: shift to an axis a distance d away

example.problem: A 3 kg solid paraboloid has a = 0.2 m and r = 0.1 m. Find I_{yy} about its mass centre.

I_{yy} = I_{zz} = (1/6) m (a^{2} + r^{2}.title: Solid paraboloid: transverse inertia at the flat face
I_{yy} = I_{zz} = (1/6) m (a^{2} + r^{2}.about: A uniform solid paraboloid has moment of inertia (1/6) m (a^{2} + r^{2}) about a diameter of its flat face (an axis through Bₒ perpendicular to x). Use it when the body pivots about its base.
assumptions: Axes through Bₒ, the centre of the flat face
Equals the mass-centre value plus m (a/3)^{2}
vars: moment of inertia about a transverse axis through Bₒ
related: parallel-axis theorem: shift to an axis a distance d away

example.problem: A 3 kg solid paraboloid (a = 0.2 m, r = 0.1 m) pivots about a diameter of its flat face. Find I_{yy} there.

V = (4/3) π r^{3}.title: Volume of a sphere
V = (4/3) π r^{3}.about: A solid sphere of radius r has volume (4/3)πr^{3}.
assumptions: r is the radius, not the diameter

example.problem: A steel ball bearing is 20 mm in diameter (ρ = 7850 kg/m^{3}). Find its volume and mass.

I_{xx} = I_{yy} = I_{zz} = (2/5) m r^{2}.title: Solid sphere: inertia about any diameter
I_{xx} = I_{yy} = I_{zz} = (2/5) m r^{2}.about: A uniform solid sphere has moment of inertia (2/5) m r^{2} about every axis through its centre. A solid half sphere has the same value about axes through Bₒ, the centre of its flat face.
assumptions: Uniform density (Earth, being denser at the core, is about 0.33 m r^{2})
About the centre; for a sphere rolling, about the contact point use (7/5) m r^{2}
vars: moment of inertia about any diameter
related: parallel-axis theorem: shift to an axis a distance d away

example.problem: A 7.26 kg shot put has radius 0.11 m. Find its moment of inertia about a diameter.

A = 4π r^{2}.title: Surface area of a sphere
A = 4π r^{2}.about: A sphere of radius r has surface area 4πr^{2}. For a thin hollow sphere, mass = areal density × A.
assumptions: Thin shell: wall thickness ≪ r

example.problem: A basketball has radius 0.12 m. Find its surface area.

I_{xx} = I_{yy} = I_{zz} = (2/3) m r^{2}.title: Thin hollow sphere: inertia about any diameter
I_{xx} = I_{yy} = I_{zz} = (2/3) m r^{2}.about: A thin uniform spherical shell has moment of inertia (2/3) m r^{2} about every axis through its centre. It is larger than the solid sphere's (2/5) m r^{2} because all the mass is at radius r.
assumptions: Wall thickness ≪ r; for a thick shell use (2/5) m (r_{o}^{5} − r_{i}^{5})/(r_{o}^{3} − r_{i}^{3})
vars: moment of inertia about any diameter

example.problem: A 0.6 kg basketball (radius 0.12 m) is modelled as a thin shell. Find its moment of inertia.

V = (2/3) π r^{3}.title: Volume of a solid half sphere
V = (2/3) π r^{3}.about: A solid hemisphere of radius r has half the volume of the sphere, (2/3)πr^{3}.
assumptions: Cut through the centre
related: mass centre above the flat face

example.problem: Find the volume of a hemispherical dome of radius 0.1 m.

y_{cm} = 3r/8.title: Mass centre of a solid half sphere
y_{cm} = 3r/8.about: The mass centre of a uniform solid hemisphere lies on its axis of symmetry, 3r/8 above Bₒ, the centre of its flat face.
assumptions: Uniform density (for a plate or shell: uniform mass per area)
Measured along y from Bₒ
A thin hemispherical shell has it at r/2 instead
vars: height of the mass centre above Bₒ

example.problem: Where is the mass centre of a solid hemisphere of radius 0.1 m?

I_{xx} = I_{zz} = (83/320) m r^{2}.title: Solid half sphere: transverse inertia at the mass centre
I_{xx} = I_{zz} = (83/320) m r^{2}.about: A uniform solid hemisphere has moment of inertia (83/320) m r^{2} about an axis through its mass centre parallel to its flat face. It is (2/5) m r^{2} about Bₒ, less m (3r/8)^{2}.
assumptions: Axes through the mass centre, 3r/8 above Bₒ
About Bₒ: (2/5) m r^{2}
vars: moment of inertia about a transverse axis through B_{cm}
related: parallel-axis theorem: shift to an axis a distance d away

example.problem: A 4 kg solid hemisphere has radius 0.1 m. Find I_{xx} about its mass centre.

I_{yy} = (2/5) m r^{2}.title: Solid half sphere: inertia about its symmetry axis
I_{yy} = (2/5) m r^{2}.about: A uniform solid hemisphere has moment of inertia (2/5) m r^{2} about its symmetry axis y, the same as a full sphere, since each half contributes equally.
assumptions: y is the axis through Bₒ and the mass centre, normal to the flat face
vars: moment of inertia about the symmetry axis

example.problem: A 4 kg solid hemisphere of radius 0.1 m spins about its symmetry axis. Find I_{yy}.

V = (4/3) π a b c.title: Volume of an ellipsoid
V = (4/3) π a b c.about: A solid ellipsoid with semi-axes a, b and c (along x, y and z) has volume (4/3)πabc. With a = b = c = r it is the sphere.
assumptions: a, b, c are semi-axes (half the full widths)

^{N}L⃗^{Q} = m^{Q} ^{N}v⃗^{Q}.title: Linear momentum of a particle
^{N}L⃗^{Q} = m^{Q} ^{N}v⃗^{Q}.about: A particle's linear (translational) momentum in frame N is its mass times its velocity in N. Newton's second law says its rate of change in N is the resultant force: F⃗ = ^{N}d^{N}L⃗/dt.
assumptions: N should be a Newtonian (inertial) frame for F⃗ = d L⃗/dt to hold
Non-relativistic speeds

^{N}L⃗^{S} = Σ_{i=1}^{n} m^{Q_{i}} ^{N}v.title: Linear momentum of a system
^{N}L⃗^{S} = Σ_{i=1}^{n} m^{Q_{i}} ^{N}v.about: The momentum of a set of particles (or a body) is the sum of their momenta, which equals the total mass times the velocity of the mass centre. So a system's momentum only depends on how its mass centre moves.
assumptions: Holds for any system of constant total mass, rigid or not
N is the frame the velocities are measured in
vars: momentum of system S in N

^{N}H⃗^{Q∕P} = ^{P}r⃗^{Q} × ^{N}L⃗^{Q}.about: A particle's angular momentum about point P in frame N is the moment of its linear momentum: the position from P to Q crossed with m ^{N}v⃗^{Q}.
assumptions: Order matters: r⃗ × L⃗, with r⃗ from P to Q
Mitiguy defines it with Q's velocity in N, whatever P is doing

example.problem: A box spins about its mass centre with ^{N}ω⃗^{B} = 2 b̂_{x} + 3 b̂_{z} rad/s; its principal inertias there are I_{xx} = 0.1, I_{yy} = 0.2, I_{zz} = 0.3 kg·m^{2}. Find ^{N}H⃗^{B∕B_{cm}}.
steps: B_{p} = B_{cm}, so the second term is 0
example.answer: ^{N}H⃗^{B∕B_{cm}} = 0.2 b̂_{x} + 0.9 b̂_{z} kg·m^{2}/s (not parallel to ω⃗)

^{N}H⃗^{B∕B_{p}} = I_{zz}^{B∕B_{p}} ^{N}.title: Angular momentum in planar motion
^{N}H⃗^{B∕B_{p}} = I_{zz}^{B∕B_{p}} ^{N}.about: For a body turning about a fixed direction b̂_{z} (planar motion, with b̂_{z} a principal axis), the inertia dyadic reduces to the scalar I_{zz}^{B∕B_{p}}. The second term accounts for B_{p} moving and is zero if B_{p} is the mass centre or at rest in N.
assumptions: b̂_{z} is a principal axis of B at B_{p} (I_{xz} = I_{yz} = 0)
I_{zz}^{B∕B_{p}} is about B_{p}
vars: moment of inertia about the b̂_{z} axis through B_{p}

example.problem: A 2 kg rod, 1.2 m long, lies along b̂_{y} from its end B_{p}. B_{p} moves at 3 n̂_{x} m/s and ω⃗ = 5 n̂_{z} rad/s. Find ^{N}H⃗^{B∕B_{p}}.

^{N}H⃗^{S∕P} = ^{N}H⃗^{S∕O} + ^{P}r⃗^{O}.title: Shifting angular momentum to another point
^{N}H⃗^{S∕P} = ^{N}H⃗^{S∕O} + ^{P}r⃗^{O}.about: Angular momentum about a new point P equals that about O plus the moment, about P, of the system's linear momentum placed at O. It is the momentum version of the moment-shift rule M⃗^{P} = M⃗^{O} + r⃗ × F⃗.
assumptions: Any system S and any two points O and P
Velocities are all in the same frame N

example.problem: A system has ^{N}H⃗^{S∕O} = 2 n̂_{z} kg·m^{2}/s and ^{N}L⃗^{S} = 4 n̂_{x} kg·m/s. P is at 0.5 n̂_{y} m from O, so ^{P}r⃗^{O} = −0.5 n̂_{y} m. Find ^{N}H⃗^{S∕P}.

^{N}H⃗^{B∕P} = ^{N}H⃗^{B∕B_{p}} + ^{P}r⃗.title: Shifting a rigid body's angular momentum
^{N}H⃗^{B∕P} = ^{N}H⃗^{B∕B_{p}} + ^{P}r⃗.about: A rigid body's angular momentum about any point P is that about a body point B_{p} plus the moment about P of its linear momentum placed at B_{p}. With B_{p} the mass centre, H⃗ about the mass centre is I⃡ · ω⃗, which makes this the usual route to H⃗ about a contact point or pivot.
assumptions: Holds for any point B_{p}: it is the shift theorem with O = B_{p}, because ^{N}H⃗ uses velocities in N
The mass centre is the usual B_{p}, where ^{N}H⃗^{B∕B_{cm}} = I⃡^{B∕B_{cm}} · ^{N}ω⃗^{B}
All velocities in N

example.problem: A 3 kg disk of radius 0.2 m rolls at 2 n̂_{x} m/s, so ω⃗ = −10 n̂_{z} rad/s. Find its angular momentum about the contact point P.

∫ F⃗ dt = ΔL⃗.title: Impulse–momentum principle
∫ F⃗ dt = ΔL⃗.about: The impulse of the resultant force over a time interval equals the change in linear momentum in a Newtonian frame. It handles collisions and short, sharp forces without knowing the force at every instant.
assumptions: N must be a Newtonian frame
F⃗ is the resultant external force on the system
Constant mass

example.problem: A 0.057 kg tennis ball arrives at 30 m/s and leaves along the same line at 40 m/s after 5 ms on the racket. Find the impulse and the average force.

∫ M⃗^{S∕O} dt = ΔH⃗^{S∕O}.title: Angular impulse–momentum principle
∫ M⃗^{S∕O} dt = ΔH⃗^{S∕O}.about: The time integral of the resultant moment about O equals the change in angular momentum about O. It holds when O is fixed in a Newtonian frame or is the system's mass centre.
assumptions: O fixed in the Newtonian frame N, or O is the mass centre
Only external moments count; internal ones cancel
If the moment is zero, angular momentum about O is conserved
vars: change in angular momentum about O

example.problem: A flywheel with I = 0.5 kg·m^{2} about its fixed axle starts at rest. A motor applies 2 N·m for 3 s. Find its final spin rate.
steps: ΔH = I ω, so ω = 6/0.5 = 12 rad/s
